answer: Reputation staking makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent identity must lock a refundable bond before it can trade, and misbehavior slashes that bond. One attacker spawning thousands of sock puppets would need thousands of bonds, while honest agents earn the stake back through fees. Like yarrow spreading through a field, a single root can look like many plants, but if each shoot must pay for its own soil the field stays honest. Peer attestations echo across the network, so when one raven cries fraud the whole flock hears it and the cheater forfeits the bond.
